'''Marcus Hutter''' (born 14 April 1967 in [[Munich]]) is a German computer scientist, professor and [[artificial intelligence]] researcher. As a senior researcher at [[DeepMind]], he studies the mathematical foundations of [[artificial general intelligence]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HomePage of Marcus Hutter |url=http://www.hutter1.net/index.htm}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite magazine |date=2023-09-07 |title=TIME100 AI 2023: Shane Legg |url=https://time.com/collection/time100-ai/6310659/shane-legg/ |access-date=2024-08-25 |magazine=Time |language=en}}</ref>

Hutter studied [[physics]] and [[computer science]] at the [[Technical University of Munich]]. In 2000, he joined [[Jürgen Schmidhuber]]'s group at the [[Dalle Molle Institute for Artificial Intelligence Research]] in [[Manno]], Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-15 |title=Marcus Hutter |url=https://www.aiandsociety.org/en/marcushutter/ |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=aiandsociety.org |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> He developed a mathematical formalism of [[artificial general intelligence]] named [[AIXI]]. He has served as a professor at the [[ANU College of Engineering, Computing and Cybernetics|College of Engineering, Computing and Cybernetics]] of the [[Australian National University]] in [[Canberra]], Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Marcus Hutter |url=https://researchers.anu.edu.au/researchers/hutter-m |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=[[Australian National University]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==

Starting in 2000, Hutter developed and published a mathematical theory of [[artificial general intelligence]], [[AIXI]], based on idealised [[intelligent agents]] and reward-motivated [[reinforcement learning]].<ref>{{cite book |author=Marcus Hutter |url=https://archive.org/details/arxiv-cs0004001 |title=A Theory of Universal Artificial Intelligence based on Algorithmic Complexity |year=2000 |bibcode=2000cs........4001H |arxiv=cs.AI/0004001}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hutter |first=Marcus |date=2013-11-28 |title=To create a super-intelligent machine, start with an equation |url=https://theconversation.com/to-create-a-super-intelligent-machine-start-with-an-equation-20756 |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=The Conversation |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> His first book ''Universal Artificial Intelligence: Sequential Decisions Based on Algorithmic Probability'' was published in 2005 by [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]].<ref>Marcus Hutter (2005). ''Universal Artificial Intelligence: Sequential Decisions Based on Algorithmic Probability''. Berlin; Heidelberg; New York: Springer. {{ISBN|9783540221395}}.</ref> Also in 2005, Hutter published with his doctoral student [[Shane Legg]] an intelligence test for artificial intelligence devices.<ref name="ns">{{Cite web |last=Graham-Rowe |first=Duncan |date=12 August 2005 |title=IQ test for AI devices gets experts thinking |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn7842-iq-test-for-ai-devices-gets-experts-thinking/ |access-date=2024-08-25 |website=New Scientist |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2009, Hutter developed and published the theory of feature reinforcement learning.<ref name="frl">{{cite journal |author=Marcus Hutter |year=2009 |title=Feature Reinforcement Learning: Part I. Unstructured MDPs |url=http://www.hutter1.net/ai/phimdpx.pdf |journal=Journal of Artificial General Intelligence |volume=1 |issue=1 |page=3 |doi=10.2478/v10229-011-0002-8 |arxiv=0906.1713 |bibcode=2009JAGI....1....3H |issn=1946-0163}}</ref> In 2014, Lattimore and Hutter published an asymptotically optimal extension of the [[AIXI]] agent.<ref name="bexp">{{cite conference |author=Tor Lattimore and Marcus Hutter |title=Algorithmic Learning Theory |chapter=Bayesian Reinforcement Learning with Exploration |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |conference=Proc. 25th International Conf. on Algorithmic Learning Theory ({ALT'14}) |year=2014|volume=8776 |pages=170–184 |chapter-url=http://www.hutter1.net/publ/pacbayes.pdf | doi=10.1007/978-3-319-11662-4_13 |hdl=1885/14709 |isbn=978-3-319-11661-7 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

An accessible podcast with [[Lex Fridman]] about his theory of [[AIXI|Universal AI]] appeared in 2021<ref name="lex">{{Cite web |last=Fridman |first=Lex |date=26 February 2020 |title=Marcus Hutter: Universal Artificial Intelligence, AIXI, and AGI |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E1AxVXt2Gv4 |via=YouTube |language=en-US}}</ref> and a more technical follow-up with Tim Nguyen in 2024 in the Cartesian Cafe.<ref name="tim">{{Cite web |last=Nguyen |first=Tim |date=10 May 2024 |title=Universal Artificial Intelligence and Solomonoff Induction |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7TgOwMW_rnk |via=YouTube |language=en-US}}</ref> His new (2024) book<ref>{{cite book |author=Marcus Hutter |title=An Introduction to Universal Artificial Intelligence |url=https://www.routledge.com/An-Introduction-to-Universal-Artificial-Intelligence/Hutter-Catt-Quarel/p/book/9781032607023 |date=2024 |publisher=Taylor & Francis |isbn=9781032607023}}</ref> also gives a more accessible introduction to Universal AI and progress in the 20 years since his first book, including a chapter on [[Superintelligence|ASI]] [[AI safety|safety]], which featured as a keynote at the inaugural workshop on AI safety in Sydney.<ref name="asi">{{Cite web |last=Hutter |first=Marcus |date=9 December 2024 |title=ASI Safety via AIXI |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qHqv3GvWBTM |via=YouTube |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Hutter Prize ==
{{Main|Hutter Prize}}
In 2006, Hutter announced the [[Hutter Prize|Hutter Prize for Lossless Compression of Human Knowledge]], with a total of €50,000 in prize money.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Chiang |first=Ted |date=2023-02-09 |title=ChatGPT Is a Blurry JPEG of the Web |url=https://www.newyorker.com/tech/annals-of-technology/chatgpt-is-a-blurry-jpeg-of-the-web |access-date=2024-08-25 |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://prize.hutter1.net|title=50'000€ Prize for Compressing Human Knowledge|author=Marcus Hutter |work=hutter1.net|access-date=29 November 2016}}</ref> In 2020, Hutter raised the prize money for the Hutter Prize to €500,000.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sagar |first=Ram |date=2020-04-07 |title=Compress Data And Win Hutter Prize Worth Half A Million Euros |url=https://analyticsindiamag.com/hutter-prize-data-compression/ |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Analytics India Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>
